evidence.chinaDemandEvidence: Build and lead a colony on the surface of an endless Wall. Manage resources and your people, develop new technologies, defend against relentless zyrex attacks, and send robo-spiders on risky expeditions. Keep the colony from collapsing – in Wall World, it's easy to fall. The Wall is a colossal structure stretching far beyond the visible horizon, hiding traces of ancient eras and unexplained phenomena within its depths. Here, among stone, metal, and darkness, humanity has been forced to build a new life – clinging to the Wall and trying to survive in a world full of threats and mysteries. Wall World Strategy is a colony sim on a sheer vertical surface, where every decision affects the stability of the system. Build and expand your base, gather resources, take care of your people, strengthen your defenses, and send expeditions into distant regions and unexplored depths. Each new step forward brings not only opportunities for growth but also new dangers. Survival depends on your foresight, your ability to manage limited resources, and your willingness to make difficult decisions. BUILD AND EXPAND THE COLONY Establish a base on the surface of the Endless Wall and gradually turn a small outpost into a large, stable, and well-defended colony. Plan the placement of key structures, develop production chains, expand living areas, and build infrastructure capable of supporting both population growth and stable operations. As your colony grows, you will need to decide how to expand, which structures to prioritize, and where to allocate resources – whether into production, housing, or defense. WITHSTAND THE THREATS The Wall is far from lifeless. In its shadows lurk zyrexes – dangerous creatures that will attack your colony again and again, testing its defenses, organization, and your ability to respond. Strengthen your defenses, secure vulnerable areas, and decide how much you can afford to invest in protection. Additional pressure comes from emergency events such as accidents, disasters, and environmental hazards. They won't destroy your colony instantly, but they will disrupt its operations and trigger cascading problems. MANAGE YOUR SOCIETY Your colony is, above all, made up of people – living, working, hoping for the future, and depending on your decisions. Monitor their condition and take into account how they react to your choices. Overpopulation, food shortages, or supply disruptions can quickly lead to declining efficiency, crisis, and riots. Caring for your people is a core part of the strategy. The state of your population determines the performance of the entire colony – its productivity and its ability to endure prolonged periods of danger. A strong and well-supported society recovers faster from attacks and moves forward with greater confidence. GATHER RESOURCES AND ADVANCE Start with basic resource extraction and gradually build a more complex economy. Explore the depths of the Wall, search for stable resource deposits, and develop the infrastructure needed to use them efficiently. Technological progress allows you to improve core systems and unlock new possibilities. Enhance resource gathering and processing, reduce costs, increase efficiency, and strengthen your colony against external threats. Some technologies accelerate infrastructure development, others improve defense, automate key processes, or expand your ability to explore new areas of the Wall. SEND OUT EXPEDITIONS To explore beyond your colony, deploy robo-spiders – specialized machines designed for scouting, resource extraction, and operations in remote areas. Send them into uncharted sectors of the Wall to expand your reach, gather resources, uncover rare discoveries, and explore areas that are too dangerous or inaccessible for humans. However, distant regions bring not only opportunities but also risks. Expeditions may encounter hostile environments, unstable terrain, unknown lifeforms, or remnants of ancient machinery whose purpose has long been forgotten. Prepare your equipment, assess the risks, and decide how far you're willing to go. EXPLORE THE DEPTHS OF THE WALL The Wall is more than just the surface your colony clings to. Beneath it lies an entire world filled with resources, forgotten technologies, and rare artifacts. Extract valuable materials, recover technological samples that can accelerate your development, and uncover unique objects that help you understand this world. As you explore, you will begin to find answers – but each discovery raises new questions about the nature of the Wall and why it became humanity's last refuge. PLAY BY YOUR OWN RULES Develop your colony in Sandbox Mode without story constraints or time pressure. Choose from different maps and difficulty levels, tailor the conditions to your liking, and keep playing for as long as you want. Zyrexes will still attack, but you can play at your own pace and experiment with different development and defense strategies. evidence.chinaDemandEvidence: In the summer of 2032, fourteen-year-old Lin Haoyang receives a box of old photographs sent by his father from Xi'an. Sorting albums, identifying faces, and completing the family tree, he slowly pieces together a century of memories of an ordinary Chinese family over six summer days. 2032. Summer. Fourteen-year-old Lin Haoyang is spending the summer alone in Shanghai. His mother is on a business trip in Japan; his father has gone back to the family home to arrange his great-grandmother's funeral. Then a box arrives from home: an empty album, a document bag, and a bundle of old black-and-white photographs. "You've got nothing better to do this summer. Sort these into albums for me." So Haoyang begins, one photograph at a time. He has never met most of the people in them, and the world they belonged to feels very far away. But every photograph, every letter, every old document points toward the story of one family. Tracing a family through old photographs · Sort the photographs: place more than 160 photographs into the right spots in the family album. · Identify the portraits: click on the people in the photographs to extract their portraits, and use the clues to identify them. · Follow the clues: read memoirs, notes, identity papers, old letters, and newspaper clippings for the details time has buried. · Complete the family tree: match the names you collect to the portraits, fill in the family tree, and untangle the relationships between generations. · Talk to the family: open your phone and ask relatives about the stories behind the photographs. · Look things up: browse Kiwi Wiki for the objects, places, and eras in the photographs—or put on a record and take your time. A century of memories, one ordinary family The story told by these old photographs runs from 1915 to 1985. A village in Hebei, an apprentice's workshop in Tianjin, the hide trade in Shanxi, an old house in Xi'an, a new life after reform and opening-up... The joys and sorrows of an ordinary Chinese family are scattered across photographs, documents, and the stories relatives tell. Across six summer days, six batches of photographs arrive. There are no countdowns and no fail states. You can spend a quiet summer afternoon looking at one photograph, getting to know one person. In the end In these old black-and-white photographs, the youth they have lost remains. And there, too, is the place we ourselves came from.
